facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against the ready view is that covenant tests, guarantee and security terms and the springing maturities of the revolver rest on the issuer's own summaries, so a definition in the executed agreements could change the headroom reading. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a turn is order intake and a narrowing loss: total backlog is USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 705 million at FY2025, trailer shipments for the nine months rose year on year, and quarterly EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters. That evidence would win if quarterly EBITDA turns positive while the backlog converts at stable prices, and it would lose if the cost base and tariffs keep gross margin thin or if the early orders prove to be pull-forward ahead of price increases, which the issuer itself notes. Two quarters of positive reported EBITDA would justify a leverage reading; a further fall in liquidity would confirm the negative one. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C02

tables.title: Contrary evidence and what would change the view

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Medium: The issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or non-GAAP reconciliation in any of the five filings, so reported EBITDA is derived from income from operations and consolidated depreciation and amortization, with impairments and asset sale gains left in. No issuer add-back bridge or adjusted measure can be shown, and the issuer's fixed charge coverage definition cannot be rebuilt from the statements. An earnings release reconciliation or the credit agreement definition would close this. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40 - Medium: Leverage multiples are not stated for FY2024 or for the periods ending 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 because reported EBITDA is not above zero, and the matching chart cells are marked not supplied. The debt stack states no cumulative leverage for the same reason. Normalised multiples are given for FY2024 only; the FY2025 normalised figure is also not above zero, and the interim windows cannot be normalised exactly. Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05 - Medium: The USD 418.6 million 2025 gain is disclosed for the year but not by quarter, and the twelve month windows ending 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 still hold part of it, so their EBITDA cannot be normalised exactly; the window ending 2026-09-30 excludes it. The split of the settlement credit between the first and third quarters of 2025 would close this gap. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C03 - Medium: The issuer states liquidity as cash plus available revolver capacity to one decimal and prints no borrowing base amount, so undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity chart are the stated liquidity less cash, not the commitment less drawings. The commitment was USD 350.0 million until 2026-08-12 and USD 300.0 million afterwards. A borrowing base certificate would close this. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C06 - Low: Several statement cells are not supplied because the filing prints a dash or no line: income from the unconsolidated entity in Q1 2026; impairment, equity in income of the unconsolidated entity, stock option proceeds, stock repurchases, debt issuance costs, acquisitions, distributions to noncontrolling interest, convertible note proceeds and other financing in some cash flow columns; and the current portion of long-term debt and two deferred income tax lines in the balance sheet. None is read as zero and every total still adds. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_wnc-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 103–106; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 95–98; 10-Q_2026-03-31_wnc-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4 - Low: Consolidated cash includes cash held in the 50% owned variable interest entity, USD 4.302 million at 2026-09-30. The 2024 annual report states no restricted cash at 2024-12-31 and 2023-12-31 and no later filing states any, so net debt uses reported cash without deducting the entity share. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2024-12-31_wnc-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 109 - Low: The revolver states no interest rate floor, so the floor cell is not supplied; the margin is stated only as a range that depends on average excess availability, so no single spread is given. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20 - Low: The segment schedule prints a dash for gross profit in the corporate and eliminations column, and the segment note and the cash flow statement differ by USD 1 thousand in H1 2026 depreciation and amortization; both are kept as printed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40 - Low: Balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not available because the 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so no interim 2025 net debt or leverage is stated; the 2025 interim income and cash flow columns are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_wnc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2 - Low: Nothing after the 2026-10-29 signing date of the latest report is established, and the report states no subsequent event, so the post-balance-sheet table records none. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 92

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is the order book. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 is 70% above year end 2025, 2027 dry van order books opened early and trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 on higher dry van and platform shipments, so earnings could recover fast enough to make the dividend and any restored buyback unremarkable and support a Low rating. Against that, truck body shipments fell 50.4% in nine months 2026, the trailer segment still lost money, and part of the order surge may be tariff-driven pull-forward. The view would move to High if the proxy statement showed a concentrated holder or entrenched board control, if dividends or buybacks were funded from the revolver while the 2028 maturity approaches, or if the executed credit documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity that was then used. It would move to Low if backlog converted into positive operating cash flow, the 2028 notes were refinanced and no further support to affiliates appeared. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings no longer cover the debt, so cash burn is the central credit risk. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, while cash interest of USD 22.82 million is a fixed claim, so interest is being paid from liquidity rather than from operations. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The maturity profile is back-ended, but the revolver springs ahead of the 2028 notes, so refinancing is the dated credit event. No principal falls due before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, yet the revolver's maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before those notes mature, 2028-07-16, less than 20 months from the as-of date. The issuer's debt note puts the Senior Notes at 92.88% of principal on third-party pricing that it says may not reflect daily market activity, and it has not decided how to address the maturity. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C06; calculation C07

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the turn may already be under way. Quarterly reported EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters, Q3 2026 trailer shipments rose 43.3% and net sales 24.8%, the issuer sold USD 150.0 million of convertible notes in 2026 after exercise of the full over-allotment option, the revolver is undrawn, and forecasters expect 2027 industry production 30.10% and 16.34% above their 2026 estimates. If backlog converts at stable prices and fixed cost is absorbed, reported EBITDA could turn positive and the 2028 refinancing would then depend mainly on market access. The view would improve on two consecutive quarters of positive reported EBITDA with positive operating cash flow, or on an extension of the 2028 notes or the revolver; it would worsen if total backlog fell back toward the USD 705 million of year end 2025, if the revolver were drawn to fund dividends, or if liquidity moved toward the USD 90 million minimum. facts.label: Credit-relevant company description
facts.text: Wabash designs, manufactures and services dry van, refrigerated, platform and tank trailers, truck bodies and composite products, and sells aftermarket parts and services through two reportable segments. facts.text: Revenue is volume-driven, cyclical, discretionary and moderately concentrated, with price increases passed on but occasionally with delay. Trailer demand follows the amount of freight to be carried, new trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 while truck body shipments fell 50.4%, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales. facts.text: Margins cannot be defended under further volume pressure or cost inflation. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the order book is the main tailwind and tariffs, truck bodies and margins are the headwinds. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The realistic downside begins with orders that are cancelled or deferred after the early 2027 order cycle, for example because customers pulled demand forward ahead of tariff price increases. The first operational break is the dry van lines that were staffed and prepared for higher 2027 production, which would run under-absorbed while truck bodies stay weak, so gross margin would stay near the 3.12% of Q3 2026 and reported EBITDA would remain negative. Free cash flow would stay near the USD 144.30 million twelve month burn or the USD 75.01 million nine-month burn, so liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last between 15.55 and 22.44 months from 2026-09-30, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date and ends before the Senior Notes could be refinanced from earnings. Management levers are limited capital spending already near USD 9.19 million for nine months, suspension of the USD 0.08 per share quarterly dividend, the unused repurchase authorization, further asset sales and cash that could be released from working capital, with receivables of USD 198.61 million and inventory of USD 195.33 million at 2026-09-30, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall through most of 2027 but not sufficient to reach the 2028 maturities without an earnings recovery or an extension. ## Request

Source readiness for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, for the credit snapshot pathway with Q3 2026 as the current period and FY2025 as the prior period. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, and which other work they cannot support.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The five supplied filings are enough to run a credit snapshot of WABASH NATIONAL Corp to Q3 2026, but not to test covenant definitions, ratings or market pricing, because no executed debt agreements, agency ratings or market quotes were supplied. Creditor protections can therefore be described only as the issuer summarises them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 91

Audited annual statements for FY2023 to FY2025 and quarterly statements through the quarter ended 2026-09-30 let net debt, liquidity and trailing twelve month figures be built from primary documents. Nothing dated after the latest filing on 2026-10-29 was supplied, so events up to the 2026-11-18 cutoff are not established.
### Key findings

Period coverage fits the pathway. Two annual reports supply FY2023 to FY2025, three quarterly reports supply Q1, Q2 and Q3 of 2026 with 2025 comparatives, and the FY2025 annual report prints quarterly sales and profit for 2025, so Q4 2025 and the twelve months to Q3 2026 can be derived without a further document. The quarterly cash flow statements are year to date, so discrete Q2 and Q3 cash flows need subtraction.

Debt disclosure is instrument level for all three debt instruments: the 4.50% unsecured senior notes due 2028, the 4.00% convertible notes due 2032 issued in July 2026, and the secured revolving credit agreement, which was amended in August 2026 to cut commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and to extend maturity to 2031. The revolver carries a minimum liquidity test of USD 90 million until a springing fixed charge coverage test takes over, and the issuer reports compliance with all covenants at the latest quarter end.

Period comparability needs care before any trend is read. The 2024 results carry a USD 450 million product liability charge in general and administrative expense, and the 2025 results book a USD 418.6 million gain against it after a settlement that insurance covered apart from a USD 30 million company contribution. The Linq business has been consolidated since 2026-01-01 with purchase accounting still provisional, although the filing states that its revenue and earnings are not material.

Several inputs that a longer pathway would use are absent: no agency rating, no trading level for the notes, no company earnings guidance, no peer set and no portfolio were supplied. The only price indication is the fair value of the notes in the debt fair value note, which rests on third-party pricing that the issuer says generally does not represent daily market activity.

Board composition, committee structure, beneficial ownership and executive pay are incorporated by reference from proxy statements that were not supplied, so Business & governance rests on the annual report's business description and executive officer list.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against the ready view is that covenant tests, guarantee and security terms and the springing maturities of the revolver rest on the issuer's own summaries, so a definition in the executed agreements could change the headroom reading. The credit agreement and both indentures would move Legal & covenants from conditional to ready, and a rating report or note quotes would do the same for Ratings & triggers and Market-implied risk. A filing after the 2026-10-29 report that changes debt, liquidity or litigation would also change the latest-quarter view.
### Limitations
- Nothing dated after 2026-10-29 was supplied, so the period to the 2026-11-18 cutoff is covered by no document.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 92
- The run settings carry no assumptions, ratings, quotes, peers, deal terms, portfolio, legal documents, earlier run or management bridge, so blank values are treated as missing, never as zero.

Earnings no longer cover the debt: reported EBITDA for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 is negative USD 100.36 million, so leverage cannot be stated and creditors depend on liquidity of USD 277.0 million against net debt of USD 470.97 million.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C01; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

Reported EBITDA of USD 366.24 million for FY2025 is inflated by a USD 418.6 million litigation gain and would be negative USD 52.36 million without it, so the reported leverage of 1.21x for that year is not a usable signal. Net debt is USD 470.97 million, against USD 281.66 million at FY2024.
Basis: calculation C05; calculation C04; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125
### Key findings

Underlying EBITDA has fallen in each year since FY2023. Reported EBITDA was USD 357.27 million in FY2023, negative USD 299.12 million in FY2024 and USD 366.24 million in FY2025, but FY2024 carries a USD 450 million product liability charge and FY2025 a USD 418.6 million gain on the same matter. Excluding both items, EBITDA falls from USD 357.27 million to USD 150.88 million to negative USD 52.36 million, as net sales fall from USD 2,536.50 million to USD 1,946.74 million to USD 1,542.75 million.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C05; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125

The loss is narrowing from a low base. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 44.92 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, negative USD 37.33 million in Q1 2026, negative USD 11.69 million in Q2 2026 and negative USD 6.42 million in Q3 2026, so the trend is better but the latest quarter is still below zero. The twelve month figure of negative USD 100.36 million still carries the weak fourth quarter of 2025.
Basis: calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40

Cash flow, not only earnings, is draining the balance sheet. Operating cash flow was negative USD 65.82 million for the nine months to 2026-09-30 even after payables and accruals rose USD 99.11 million, and capital spending of USD 9.19 million was small; USD 39.72 million of asset sale proceeds and the convertible notes bridged the gap. Cash interest of USD 22.82 million over the twelve months is a fixed claim on that same cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C03; calculation C12

Debt at carrying value is USD 540.26 million, USD 9.74 million below principal of USD 550.0 million, and consists of USD 400.0 million of 4.50% unsecured senior notes due 2028, USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible notes due 2032 issued in July 2026 and an undrawn revolver. Net debt rose USD 60.04 million in the nine months because cash burn, fees and dividends exceeded asset sale proceeds; the convertible notes repaid revolver borrowings and changed the debt mix more than the net total.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C13

Maturities are back-ended but the revolver springs. No principal falls due before 2028-10-15, when USD 400.0 million of senior notes mature; the revolver was cut from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and extended to 2031 in August 2026, but it matures 91 days before the senior notes or the convertible notes mature, so the 2028 refinancing governs access to the only committed liquidity.

Liquidity of USD 277.0 million is the issuer's cash plus available revolver capacity, of which USD 69.29 million is cash; it was USD 165.1 million at 2026-03-31 and USD 235.3 million at FY2025, and rose after the convertible notes repaid revolver borrowings rather than because operations produced cash.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_wnc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C06

Funding that is not debt is mixed. Customer deposits fell from USD 26.45 million at FY2025 to USD 17.99 million and chassis converter pool financing fell from USD 59.60 million to USD 21.73 million, both inside other accrued liabilities, while accounts payable rose from USD 145.74 million to USD 246.18 million, so suppliers are funding more of the business than customers are.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a turn is order intake and a narrowing loss: total backlog is USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 705 million at FY2025, trailer shipments for the nine months rose year on year, and quarterly EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters. That evidence would win if quarterly EBITDA turns positive while the backlog converts at stable prices, and it would lose if the cost base and tariffs keep gross margin thin or if the early orders prove to be pull-forward ahead of price increases, which the issuer itself notes. Two quarters of positive reported EBITDA would justify a leverage reading; a further fall in liquidity would confirm the negative one.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C02
### Limitations

- Reported EBITDA is derived from statement lines because the five filings state no EBITDA or non-GAAP reconciliation; impairments and asset sale gains stay in it, and the issuer's own fixed charge coverage definition cannot be rebuilt.

- The 2025 product liability gain is disclosed for the year but not by quarter, so the twelve month windows ending 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30, which still hold part of it, cannot be normalised exactly.
- Interim figures are unaudited, and the 2025 interim comparatives come from the 2026 reports because the 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- Medium: The issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or non-GAAP reconciliation in any of the five filings, so reported EBITDA is derived from income from operations and consolidated depreciation and amortization, with impairments and asset sale gains left in. No issuer add-back bridge or adjusted measure can be shown, and the issuer's fixed charge coverage definition cannot be rebuilt from the statements. An earnings release reconciliation or the credit agreement definition would close this.

- Medium: Leverage multiples are not stated for FY2024 or for the periods ending 2026-03-31, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 because reported EBITDA is not above zero, and the matching chart cells are marked not supplied. The debt stack states no cumulative leverage for the same reason. Normalised multiples are given for FY2024 only; the FY2025 normalised figure is also not above zero, and the interim windows cannot be normalised exactly.
Basis: calculation C04; calculation C05

- Medium: The USD 418.6 million 2025 gain is disclosed for the year but not by quarter, and the twelve month windows ending 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 still hold part of it, so their EBITDA cannot be normalised exactly; the window ending 2026-09-30 excludes it. The split of the settlement credit between the first and third quarters of 2025 would close this gap.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C03

- Medium: The issuer states liquidity as cash plus available revolver capacity to one decimal and prints no borrowing base amount, so undrawn committed facilities in the liquidity chart are the stated liquidity less cash, not the commitment less drawings. The commitment was USD 350.0 million until 2026-08-12 and USD 300.0 million afterwards. A borrowing base certificate would close this.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C06

- Low: Several statement cells are not supplied because the filing prints a dash or no line: income from the unconsolidated entity in Q1 2026; impairment, equity in income of the unconsolidated entity, stock option proceeds, stock repurchases, debt issuance costs, acquisitions, distributions to noncontrolling interest, convertible note proceeds and other financing in some cash flow columns; and the current portion of long-term debt and two deferred income tax lines in the balance sheet. None is read as zero and every total still adds.

- Low: Consolidated cash includes cash held in the 50% owned variable interest entity, USD 4.302 million at 2026-09-30. The 2024 annual report states no restricted cash at 2024-12-31 and 2023-12-31 and no later filing states any, so net debt uses reported cash without deducting the entity share.
- Low: The revolver states no interest rate floor, so the floor cell is not supplied; the margin is stated only as a range that depends on average excess availability, so no single spread is given.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

- Low: The segment schedule prints a dash for gross profit in the corporate and eliminations column, and the segment note and the cash flow statement differ by USD 1 thousand in H1 2026 depreciation and amortization; both are kept as printed.

- Low: Balance sheets at 2025-03-31, 2025-06-30 and 2025-09-30 are not available because the 2025 quarterly reports were not supplied, so no interim 2025 net debt or leverage is stated; the 2025 interim income and cash flow columns are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports.
- Low: Nothing after the 2026-10-29 signing date of the latest report is established, and the report states no subsequent event, so the post-balance-sheet table records none.

spans.text: # WABASH NATIONAL Corp business and governance
## Request

Business and governance for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, issuer history and transactions through the Q3 2026 report, and sponsor and governance behaviour as far as the five supplied filings show it.
## Sources

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

WABASH NATIONAL Corp is a publicly listed trailer and truck-body manufacturer with no identified controlling owner or sponsor, so creditors rely on a cyclical operating business and on a board that kept paying dividends through a loss-making 2026.

Sponsor and governance risk is Medium. Repurchases fell from USD 76.21 million in FY2023 to USD 33.77 million in FY2025 and none were made in the first nine months of 2026, and the audit opinion is unqualified. Against that, dividends of USD 10.03 million were still paid in nine months 2026 against an operating loss of USD 97.68 million, USD 150.0 million of convertible debt was added in July 2026 and the revolver was cut from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million.
### Key findings

No sponsor or controlling shareholder is identified, which removes leveraged-buyout style extraction risk but also means no sponsor equity support is documented. The issuer is a Delaware company listed on the New York Stock Exchange with one class of common stock, and beneficial ownership percentages and board control rights sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so concentration of control is not established.

The operating model is cyclical equipment manufacturing, and the Parts & Services business that management positions as less cyclical is still too small to offset the trailer loss. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales and the Transportation Solutions segment lost USD 58.79 million at the operating line, while Parts & Services earned USD 15.52 million on 15.53% of external sales.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C10

Order intake has turned sharply upward but is not yet earnings. Total backlog was USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 705 million at 2025 year end, and management attributes the rise to orders exceeding shipments and an early 2027 dry van order cycle. The filing adds that some orders may reflect customers ordering ahead of tariff-related price increases and that backlog can change or be cancelled.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

Customer concentration is moderate. The five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales against 42% in FY2024, no customer exceeded 10% in FY2025 after one reached 15% in FY2024, and sales go through factory-direct accounts and independent dealers with international sales under 10%.

Shareholder returns have been scaled back but not stopped, which is mixed behaviour for creditors. In FY2025 dividends and repurchases together of USD 47.55 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 11.67 million while cash fell by USD 83.56 million, and in nine months 2026 dividends of USD 10.03 million were paid while operating cash flow was negative USD 65.82 million. USD 93.2 million of repurchase authorisation remains until February 2027, and the filings do not state the funding source of either payment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 97–98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C07; calculation C10

The July and August 2026 transactions extended maturities but added debt and tightened the revolver. The issuer sold USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2032 and repaid revolver borrowings, then cut revolver commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million and moved the stated maturity from 2027 to 2031. The revolver's stated maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, which is 2028-07-16, and no final decision on those notes is disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C06

Affiliate and venture exposure is small today but carries contingent claims. The issuer now owns Linq outright after funding it through a note, holds 20% stakes in two venture-lab companies, guarantees a counterparty's equipment lease for 24 months, and has maximum exposure of USD 12.4 million on the UpLabs arrangement and USD 5.8 million on FreightVana. The partner in the Wabash Parts joint venture holds a put right that would require the issuer to buy its 50% interest at a valuation that is not disclosed.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 109–110; calculation C01

Reporting quality is adequate and creditor-adverse transactions are not found in the five filings. The auditor gave an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 statements and on internal control, disclosure controls were reported effective at 2026-09-30, and no exchange, consent solicitation, covenant waiver, priming or sponsor fee appears in them. The 2024 jury award of USD 450 million, settled in 2025 with a USD 30 million company contribution, shows that litigation can create a very large claim before insurance and appeals.

Senior management continuity is a watch item. A new chief financial officer was appointed on 2024-09-01, new chief operating and chief commercial officers on 2025-01-15, and a transition agreement dated 2026-04-08 with the executive listed as chief growth officer in the annual report has terms that were not supplied, so continuity of the team that must deal with the 2028 notes is not established.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is the order book. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million at 2026-09-30 is 70% above year end 2025, 2027 dry van order books opened early and trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 on higher dry van and platform shipments, so earnings could recover fast enough to make the dividend and any restored buyback unremarkable and support a Low rating. Against that, truck body shipments fell 50.4% in nine months 2026, the trailer segment still lost money, and part of the order surge may be tariff-driven pull-forward. The view would move to High if the proxy statement showed a concentrated holder or entrenched board control, if dividends or buybacks were funded from the revolver while the 2028 maturity approaches, or if the executed credit documents showed wide restricted-payment capacity that was then used. It would move to Low if backlog converted into positive operating cash flow, the 2028 notes were refinanced and no further support to affiliates appeared.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting, which holds director independence, committee membership, beneficial ownership and the related-person policy, was not supplied, so the Medium rating rests on documented behaviour and a concentrated holder or weak board independence would raise it.

- The executed credit agreement and both indentures were not supplied, so capacity for dividends, repurchases, investments and extra debt is known only from issuer summaries, and the reading that shareholder returns are mixed rather than adverse could change once the baskets are read.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21
- Terms of the 2026-04-08 transition agreement and executive pay are not disclosed, so management continuity is judged only from appointment dates.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_wnc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 50
- Customer-level pricing, contract length and the share of backlog under long-term agreements are not disclosed, so the quality of the USD 1,198 million backlog cannot be tested.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The main new debt issue is the USD 150.0 million of 4.00% convertible senior unsecured notes due 2032, completed on 2026-07-20 after the initial purchasers exercised a USD 20.0 million option on 2026-07-16. The notes are guaranteed by the subsidiaries that guarantee the 4.50% Senior Notes, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 16.75 per share, a 32.50% premium to the USD 12.64 closing price on 2026-07-15, cannot be redeemed before 2029-08-06 except in a cleanup redemption, and convert into about 21.98% of the shares now outstanding if every holder converted at the initial rate. The net proceeds were used primarily to repay revolver borrowings, and the revolver had no amounts outstanding at 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05

The revolving credit agreement was amended twice. The Fifth Amendment on 2026-07-14 allowed up to USD 150.0 million of convertible notes as additional permitted debt. The Sixth Amendment on 2026-08-12 cut commitments from USD 350.0 million to USD 300.0 million, moved the scheduled maturity from 2027-09-23 to 2031-08-12 subject to earlier tests tied to other debt, kept a USD 175 million accordion and raised the margin range over term SOFR from 1.25% to 1.75% to 1.50% to 2.00%. ### Overall governance view

Overall, WABASH NATIONAL Corp presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is the continued payment of dividends and the earlier repurchases while operating cash flow was weak, which matters because cash leaves ahead of a 2028 refinancing and implies a small, mixed drain rather than extraction. Countervailing evidence is the absence of any sponsor, fee, exchange or priming history, an unqualified audit opinion and the USD 1,198 million backlog. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and the terms of the 2026 transition agreement. Business & governance completed with limitations. Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium. Key gaps: board and ownership detail, restricted payment capacity and management transition terms.

spans.text: # WABASH NATIONAL Corp fundamental credit
## Request

Fundamental credit for WABASH NATIONAL Corp (wnc-879526), as of 2026-11-18, under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the integrated credit view of business risk, financial profile, refinancing and downside, built from the five supplied filings and the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_wnc-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 2024-12-31 | 2025-02-18 | 1a025c9bb1343e50a890ef3abdb7bc82f8350deb4260b26b780f4cd4a1a37d5a | Earlier statement of the 2021 Senior Notes and the first description of the Linq and Wabash Parts ventures |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 2025-12-31 | 2026-02-18 | 25e9eafe1bd11c2f7033419f3855de2383b2af56457fb8eef60df933d5308887 | Industry and competition, customers, raw materials, FY2025 cash flows, debt fair value, product liability settlement, segment results |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_wnc-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-03-31 | 2026-05-01 | 392508e6cf5b8272341fb63e31c50c5bf0ca033614f351593d562550c0787cfb | Repurchase status and the Q1 2026 events |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_wnc-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 | 2026-07-29 | 8fc264a4956462decf16c9631e64d8d3f15ae9e2762136252a37aa538d5acdb9 | Fifth Amendment to the revolver and the convertible notes subsequent event |

| Supplied analysis | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | b8965f41421537265b543932c69c9e32645f786406cf40a9244d6d8c8494575a | Source dates, the five-filing set and the absence of ratings, quotes, peers and legal documents |

| Financial foundation | CP-1 | 74bbb9a256087af64d0abbe33274a36e052179db6f84b65c9ac30697a8921016 | Reported EBITDA, free cash flow, net debt, liquidity, maturities and cash interest; no figure was recomputed except where a calculation below says so |

No external sources were used.
## Findings
### Bottom line

WABASH NATIONAL Corp is a cyclical manufacturer in an earnings trough whose creditors rely on liquidity and back-ended maturities rather than on operating cash flow, so the credit hinges on converting a rebuilt order book into cash before the 2028 refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, yet issuer-stated liquidity is USD 277.0 million and no principal falls due before 2028-10-15, when USD 400 million of Senior Notes mature. The revolver can mature 91 days earlier, so the committed liquidity that bridges the trough is tied to the same refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11
### Key findings

Earnings no longer cover the debt, so cash burn is the central credit risk. Reported EBITDA was negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30, while cash interest of USD 22.82 million is a fixed claim, so interest is being paid from liquidity rather than from operations. The loss is narrowing, with quarterly reported EBITDA improving from negative USD 44.92 million in Q4 2025 to negative USD 6.42 million in Q3 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

Liquidity is adequate for now but was rebuilt with new debt and asset sales rather than by operations. Issuer-stated liquidity was USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 235.3 million at 2025 year end, after USD 150.0 million of convertible notes and USD 39.72 million of asset sale proceeds in nine months, while net debt rose USD 60.04 million to USD 470.97 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C11

The maturity profile is back-ended, but the revolver springs ahead of the 2028 notes, so refinancing is the dated credit event. No principal falls due before the USD 400 million 4.50% Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15, yet the revolver's maturity is the earliest of several dates, one of which is 91 days before those notes mature, 2028-07-16, less than 20 months from the as-of date. The issuer's debt note puts the Senior Notes at 92.88% of principal on third-party pricing that it says may not reflect daily market activity, and it has not decided how to address the maturity.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; calculation C06; calculation C07

Margins are the weakest dimension, because cost has risen faster than sales while volumes recovered. Gross margin fell from 19.64% in FY2023 to 1.64% in nine months 2026, and the Transportation Solutions segment's gross result moved by negative USD 47.61 million in nine months although trailer shipments rose 13.4%, which the issuer attributes to material cost, labour and overhead, truck body mix and production-readiness cost brought forward from 2027.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–52; calculation C02; calculation C04

Order intake is the strongest support, but it is not yet earnings. Twelve-month backlog of USD 1,114 million equals 73.37% of last twelve months net sales against 37.34% at 2025 year end, and total backlog of USD 1,198 million is 70% above year end. The issuer opened its 2027 dry van orders early, but it also says some orders may be ahead of tariff-related price increases and that backlog can be changed or cancelled.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation C03

Business risk sits in new trailers, with limited offset from parts and services. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales, Parts & Services was 15.53% of external sales and earned USD 15.52 million, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales with none above 10%, so concentration is moderate but cyclicality is not diversified away.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

Financial policy is mixed and the book equity cushion is thin. Dividends of USD 10.03 million were paid in nine months 2026 against an operating loss of USD 97.68 million, repurchases stopped in 2026 but USD 93.2 million of authorization remains, and tangible equity was USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30; no sponsor, exchange or priming transaction is documented.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

Cost and capex flexibility partly offsets the weak margins. Capital spending including revenue generating assets was USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026 against USD 103.74 million in FY2023, two plants were idled and Goshen was sold for about USD 17.8 million, and operating lease payments of USD 33.69 million and raw material commitments of USD 55.81 million are modest next to liquidity, so cash can be preserved if volumes disappoint.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01; calculation C11

The primary downside path is backlog failing to convert while fixed cost has been added for 2027 volumes. At the last twelve months free cash flow burn, liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last 15.55 months from 2026-09-30, and at the nine-month 2026 burn 22.44 months, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date; this is arithmetic before dividends, not a forecast.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the turn may already be under way. Quarterly reported EBITDA losses have narrowed for three consecutive quarters, Q3 2026 trailer shipments rose 43.3% and net sales 24.8%, the issuer sold USD 150.0 million of convertible notes in 2026 after exercise of the full over-allotment option, the revolver is undrawn, and forecasters expect 2027 industry production 30.10% and 16.34% above their 2026 estimates. If backlog converts at stable prices and fixed cost is absorbed, reported EBITDA could turn positive and the 2028 refinancing would then depend mainly on market access. The view would improve on two consecutive quarters of positive reported EBITDA with positive operating cash flow, or on an extension of the 2028 notes or the revolver; it would worsen if total backlog fell back toward the USD 705 million of year end 2025, if the revolver were drawn to fund dividends, or if liquidity moved toward the USD 90 million minimum.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08; calculation C11
### Limitations

- The issuer's covenant definition of liquidity, its borrowing base and its fixed charge coverage definition were not supplied, so headroom against the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test cannot be measured and the runway illustrations of 15.55 months and 22.44 months could be longer or shorter in practice.

- The filings give no company guidance, rating or trading level, so the outlook rests on third-party industry forecasts and on the debt note's fair value of the Senior Notes, which the issuer says may not reflect daily market activity.
- Backlog is stated without customer, price or margin detail, so the conversion of USD 1,198 million of orders into cash earnings could be weaker than the revenue coverage ratio suggests.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67
- No guarantor and non-guarantor financial information is printed, so the structural position of the unsecured notes behind non-guarantor subsidiaries and the secured revolver cannot be sized.
### Strengths and weaknesses
The credit has five supports that matter, ranked by how directly they reduce default pressure over the next two years.

- Liquidity and the absence of principal due before 2028 give the issuer time to reach positive cash flow. Issuer-stated liquidity of USD 277.0 million at 2026-09-30 and a debt stack with no principal until 2028-10-15 mean that interest and operating burn can be funded for some time, which lowers near-term default pressure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

- The order book recovered sharply, which supports 2027 volumes and operating leverage. Total backlog of USD 1,198 million, 70% above year end, and twelve-month backlog covering 73.37% of last twelve months net sales mean that revenue visibility is better than a year ago, provided orders convert and are not cancelled.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation C03

- Cost and capex flexibility allows cash to be preserved. Capital spending fell to USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026, two plants were idled and Goshen sold, and few fixed commitments sit outside debt, so management has levers if volumes disappoint.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 63–65; calculation C01

- Customer and channel concentration is moderate. The five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales and none exceeded 10%, with sales split between factory-direct accounts and independent dealers, so the loss of one account would not break the credit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28

- Governance does not add event risk. No sponsor, exchange offer, priming or fee leakage is documented, the audit opinion is unqualified and controls are reported effective, which limits event risk for creditors.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)
The credit has five constraints, ranked by how directly they raise default or refinancing risk.

- Earnings and free cash flow are negative. Reported EBITDA of negative USD 100.36 million and free cash flow of negative USD 144.30 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 mean that no leverage multiple exists and that debt service depends on liquidity, which raises refinancing risk with every quarter of burn.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

- Margins are very thin and falling in the trailer segment. Gross margin of 1.64% in nine months 2026 against 19.64% in FY2023, and a negative USD 47.61 million move in trailer segment gross result despite higher shipments, mean that volume recovery alone may not restore profit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C02; calculation C04

- The 2028 refinancing is the dated event and the revolver springs ahead of it. USD 400 million of Senior Notes mature on 2028-10-15 and the revolver can mature on 2028-07-16, so committed liquidity and the largest maturity fall in the same window.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; calculation C06

- Tangible equity is thin while dividends continue. Tangible equity of USD 2.21 million at 2026-09-30 leaves almost no book cushion under USD 550.0 million of debt principal, and USD 10.03 million of dividends were paid in nine months 2026 despite an operating loss.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

- Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product with a small offset. New trailers were 73.9% of nine-month 2026 net sales and Parts & Services only 15.53% of external sales, so the parts business cannot yet cushion a trailer trough.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41
### Credit-relevant company description

Wabash designs, manufactures and services dry van, refrigerated, platform and tank trailers, truck bodies and composite products, and sells aftermarket parts and services through two reportable segments. Last twelve months net sales were USD 1,518.33 million, sold through factory-direct accounts to large fleets and through independent dealers, so cash flow follows fleet replacement cycles rather than contracted recurring revenue. The business model supports debt service only when trailer orders are strong: backlog gives visibility for twelve months, but orders can be changed or cancelled and the parts and services business that management expects to be less cyclical is small.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–10; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 66; calculation C01
### Ownership and group structure

Wabash is a publicly listed company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor identified, so there is no sponsor backstop and no sponsor-driven recapitalisation risk, and the governance rating is Medium because shareholder returns continued through losses. The Senior Notes and Convertible Notes are guaranteed by domestic restricted subsidiaries and rank behind a revolver secured on substantially all personal property of the borrowers and guarantors, while the notes are structurally junior to any debt of subsidiaries that do not guarantee them, such as foreign subsidiaries, but no such debt and no guarantor financial information is printed to size that.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–22
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is volume-driven, cyclical, discretionary and moderately concentrated, with price increases passed on but occasionally with delay. Trailer demand follows the amount of freight to be carried, new trailer shipments rose 13.4% in nine months 2026 while truck body shipments fell 50.4%, and the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales. Because pricing power is limited by customers that know lifecycle costs and by imports, volume recovery supports revenue but margin recovery depends on cost, which is why revenue durability is judged average and margin stability weak.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins cannot be defended under further volume pressure or cost inflation. Gross margin was 3.12% in Q3 2026 against 4.12% in Q3 2025 even though net sales rose 24.8%, because material cost, labour and overhead rose with volume, truck body mix and low production volumes hurt profitability, and dry van lines were staffed for 2027 volumes ahead of the production they are meant to serve. Operating leverage should work in reverse if volumes recover, but fixed cost, input cost and tariff exposure on steel, aluminum and components mean that the benefit is not quantified in the filings and credit cannot rely on it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 68; calculation C02; calculation C09
### Capital intensity and FCF conversion

Capital intensity is low and flexible, but EBITDA does not translate into free cash flow because EBITDA is negative. Capital spending was USD 9.19 million in nine months 2026, receivables rose USD 78.1 million and days sales outstanding were 38 days against 35 days a year earlier, while payables and accrued liabilities rose USD 99.1 million, so suppliers funded the working capital build; interest payments of USD 24.18 million fall due in 2027 on fixed-rate notes. Free cash flow before dividends and acquisitions was negative USD 75.01 million for the nine months, so debt service, deleveraging and refinancing support all depend on the earnings recovery.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; calculation C01; calculation C09; calculation C11
### Competitive forces
Competition matters for credit only where it affects margin, cash flow or refinancing capacity. Each force is assessed on that basis.

- Rivalry is intense and price-sensitive. Trailer makers compete on quality, customer relationships, technology and price, and other makers pursue composite sidewalls that compete directly with the issuer's own panels, which limits pricing power and keeps margins thin.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13

- The threat from new entrants is mainly imports. A coalition including Wabash petitioned in November 2025 on van-type trailer imports from China, Canada and Mexico; duty orders now cover China while Canada and Mexico remain pending, so relief from import pressure is partial and not quantified.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 72

- Substitution risk is mainly composite sidewalls from competitors against the issuer's own panels and the option for cautious fleets to defer purchases; the filings give no data on trailer age or deferral, so the effect on volumes is not established.

- Buyer power is moderate. Large fleets know lifecycle costs, the five largest customers were 35% of FY2025 net sales and the largest was 15% in FY2024, so buyers can hold back orders and press price when freight is weak.

- Supplier power is meaningful. A limited number of suppliers provide steel coil, aluminum, axles, suspensions and tires, shortages or tariffs raise cost, and increases are passed on with delay, which compresses margin when prices rise.
### Macro and policy factors

Political and regulatory factors are material: tariffs and trade remedies affect material cost, supply chains, competitive conditions and customer purchasing, and the issuer says recent orders may reflect customers buying ahead of tariff-related price increases, which could pull demand forward and then leave a gap. Economic factors are material because the freight cycle sets trailer demand: the 2025 annual report described a continuing freight recession, while the latest quarterly report cites improving freight market fundamentals and accumulated replacement needs. Social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: a rebuilt order book, liquidity of USD 277.0 million with no principal until 2028-10-15, and low capital needs give the credit time and flexibility, which lowers near-term default pressure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 66–67; calculation C01

Weaknesses: negative EBITDA and free cash flow, gross margin of 1.64%, thin tangible equity of USD 2.21 million and a 73.9% share of new trailers in sales constrain debt service and make the credit dependent on a cyclical recovery.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02

Opportunities: converting backlog at stable prices, absorbing the fixed cost added for 2027 volumes, and trade remedies on imports could restore positive EBITDA and open the 2028 refinancing on better terms.

Threats: tariff pull-forward followed by cancellations, further weakness in truck bodies, input cost inflation and an unaddressed 2028 maturity with a springing revolver could drain liquidity before earnings recover.
### Financial profile and credit quality

The business profile is adequate but cyclical. Scale is average at USD 1,518.33 million of last twelve months net sales, the competitive position rests on patented panel technology and a dealer network but earns thin margins, and diversification is limited by the 73.9% share of new trailers. The financial profile is weak and improving only at the margin: cost and capex flexibility is average, margin stability is weak, free cash flow stability is weak, liquidity is average because USD 277.0 million is meaningful but burn and a USD 40 million availability block remain, ability to refinance is average because the 2026 convertible notes show market access while the 2028 notes are unaddressed, and financial policy is average because dividends continue but there is no sponsor and no creditor-adverse transaction. The main supports are liquidity, back-ended maturities and the order book; the main constraints are negative cash flow and the springing revolver; the trend is narrowing losses; and the missing datapoints are the borrowing base, covenant definitions, an issuer EBITDA and any rating or trading level.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_wnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C01; calculation C11
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the order book is the main tailwind and tariffs, truck bodies and margins are the headwinds. Forecasters expect 2026 United States trailer production 3% and 5% above 2025 and 2027 production 30.10% and 16.34% above their 2026 estimates, backlog supports early 2027 production, and duty orders on Chinese imports are in force, but part of the order surge may be tariff-driven, truck body shipments fell 50.4% in nine months 2026, and the issuer is carrying production-readiness cost ahead of volumes. Over three to five years the same forecasters expect production in 2029 to be 58.67% and 47.52% above their 2026 estimates, which the issuer calls generally consistent with historical levels, so a recovery would restore volume, but the forecasts have been revised before and the filing says actual production may differ materially.
### Downside scenario

The realistic downside begins with orders that are cancelled or deferred after the early 2027 order cycle, for example because customers pulled demand forward ahead of tariff price increases. The first operational break is the dry van lines that were staffed and prepared for higher 2027 production, which would run under-absorbed while truck bodies stay weak, so gross margin would stay near the 3.12% of Q3 2026 and reported EBITDA would remain negative. Free cash flow would stay near the USD 144.30 million twelve month burn or the USD 75.01 million nine-month burn, so liquidity above the USD 90 million minimum liquidity test would last between 15.55 and 22.44 months from 2026-09-30, which brackets the 2028-07-16 revolver date and ends before the Senior Notes could be refinanced from earnings. Management levers are limited capital spending already near USD 9.19 million for nine months, suspension of the USD 0.08 per share quarterly dividend, the unused repurchase authorization, further asset sales and cash that could be released from working capital, with receivables of USD 198.61 million and inventory of USD 195.33 million at 2026-09-30, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity shortfall through most of 2027 but not sufficient to reach the 2028 maturities without an earnings recovery or an extension.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C05; calculation C11
### Overall credit view

Overall, WABASH NATIONAL Corp presents an adequate but highly cyclical business profile supported by a rebuilt order book, back-ended maturities and USD 277.0 million of liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by negative earnings, a gross margin of 1.64% and tangible equity of USD 2.21 million. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to free cash flow of negative USD 144.30 million over the last twelve months. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on converting backlog into positive reported EBITDA and operating cash flow before the revolver can mature on 2028-07-16, and on market access for USD 400 million of Senior Notes. The primary downside path is backlog failing to convert while fixed cost has been added for 2027 volumes. A comparison with sector peers is not established because no peer set was supplied. Further analysis would require the borrowing base, covenant definitions and executed credit documents, an issuer EBITDA, guidance, ratings and trading levels. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: the 2028 refinancing and the springing revolver maturity before earnings recover.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_wnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C01; calculation C11
